Steady Performance for Canadian Automotive Trade in First Quarter

The Canadian automotive industry reported stable trade figures for the first quarter of 2024, according to data released this week by the Department of Industry and Commerce. Automotive exports totaled $21.3 billion from January to March, closely matching last year’s figures for the same period. Imports of vehicles and automotive parts reached $19.7 billion, showing a modest 1.2% increase from Q1 2023.

Industry leaders in Ontario and Quebec, Canada’s major automotive hubs, say the numbers reflect consistent demand and production capacity across North America. “We are seeing steady orders from the United States, our largest trading partner, as well as a gradual uptick in shipments to Mexico,” noted Lisa Chartrand, spokesperson for the Canadian Association of Vehicle Manufacturers (CAVM). “Supply chains remain resilient, and plants are operating at expected levels.”

Analysts attribute the stability to ongoing consumer demand for both passenger vehicles and light trucks. “There’s a healthy appetite for both traditional models and newer electric options,” said Mark Frasier, senior analyst at Northern Market Insights. “With inventories and logistics largely normalized, manufacturers are able to meet dealer needs without significant delays.”

Local unions also report regular activity at assembly plants. “Our members are working steady shifts, and we’re pleased to see no major disruptions or overtime surges,” said John Pelletier, regional chair of the Auto Workers Union.

Notably, smaller Canadian suppliers such as Maple Ridge Components and Northland Auto Tech have maintained their export volumes. The Canadian Border Services Agency confirmed that cross-border shipments have moved without incident.

Government officials say they will continue to monitor sector performance but currently anticipate no significant changes. “The industry is in a good place,” said Deputy Minister Elena Drummond. “We expect this trend of stability to continue throughout the year.”
